aboutH2: Orchard Recovery Center: Private Addiction Treatment on Bowen Island, BC
intro: At the Orchard Recovery Center, a range of treatment options is available to cater to your specific needs. Depending on your requirements, you can choose from a variety of flexible lengths of stay, starting with a 12-day introduction to treatment that includes detoxification and stabilization. This program is designed to provide you with a comprehensive foundation for recovery. Following this, you have the option of 28 or 42-day programs to build on this foundation and further enhance your recovery process.

The Orchard Recovery Center understands that every individual is unique, and hence, their journey to recovery may differ. Therefore, they provide a diverse range of treatment options to cater to each person’s personal needs. The 12-day introduction to treatment, which includes detoxification and stabilization, is an ideal starting point for individuals who require immediate assistance. This program aims to provide a solid foundation for recovery and help individuals transition into longer-term programs.

pillars.title: A Former Resort in the Bowen Island Rainforest
pillars.body: The Orchard sits on several rural acres off Grafton Road, a short drive from the ferry dock at Snug Cove. It was once a four-star resort. Clients sleep in a separate residence building surrounded by forest and fields, in mostly shared rooms with fireplaces and queen beds, and spend the day at the recovery campus, where meals, counselling, the doctors' offices and a 2,800 square foot gym are. There is a seasonal pool from May to September, a vegetable garden that supplies the kitchen, and walks around the island's lakes and forest trails. Eagles and deer turn up often.

pillars.title: A Year of Check-Ins and an Alumni Community
pillars.body: Before discharge, each client works out an aftercare plan with their counsellor and recovery coach, and the clinical team reviews it. Alumni benefits are included with the 28 and 42-day programs. Graduates get weekly and then monthly check-ups for a full year, and they can call the centre for support at any hour. There is a daily online check-in meeting from Monday to Friday and weekly alumni meetings on Zoom. Friends of the Orchard meetings also run in person in Calgary and Victoria. The centre's smartphone app keeps people in touch after they go home.

pillars.title: Addiction Physicians, a Psychiatrist and Counsellors
pillars.body: Lorinda Strang co-founded the Orchard in 2002 and is still its Executive Director. Dr. Máire Durnin, an addiction medicine physician, is Medical Director. She works with psychiatrist Dr. Adam Chodkiewicz and several addiction doctors who also practise at St. Paul's Hospital and elsewhere in the Lower Mainland. Nurses are on site during office hours and overnight. Each client has a primary counsellor, many with a master's degree in social work or counselling, plus a recovery coach who has at least two years of recovery. All programming is run by staff, and the program takes no more than 25 clients at a time.

overview: The Orchard is committed to eradicating the stigma of addiction and creating a sustainable culture of recovery. They focus on building strong communities of recovery that make meaningful contributions to society as a whole. As leaders in the recovery advocacy movement in Canada, they celebrate recovery and strive to raise awareness.

The Orchard understands that addiction affects individuals and communities, and they aim to break the cycle of shame and stigma surrounding addiction. Through their programs and services, they create a supportive environment where individuals can heal and thrive. Their approach to recovery centers around building strong communities that offer support, encouragement, and hope.

The Orchard’s commitment to advocacy and awareness-raising aims to ensure that everyone has access to the support they need to achieve long-term recovery. They believe that by fostering these communities, they can create a ripple effect of positive change that extends beyond the individual and impacts society as a whole.

In conclusion, The Orchard is dedicated to creating a sustainable culture of recovery and empowering individuals. By building strong communities and leading the recovery advocacy movement in Canada, they celebrate recovery and strive to create a future where everyone has access to the support they need to achieve a healthy, fulfilling life.

location.heading: Orchard Recovery Center in Bowen Island, British Columbia
location.intro: Orchard Recovery Center is at 811 Grafton Road on Bowen Island, a forested island in Howe Sound that is part of Metro Vancouver, and clients reach it on the 20-minute BC Ferries crossing from Horseshoe Bay in West Vancouver to Snug Cove. From downtown Vancouver the trip takes about an hour including the ferry, and it is roughly an hour and a half from Surrey, two and a half to three hours from Nanaimo on Vancouver Island by way of the Departure Bay ferry, and about four hours from Victoria with two ferry crossings.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Orchard Recovery Center cost?
faqs.a: Recovery.com lists estimated costs of $11,000 for the 12-day introduction, $21,500 for 28 days and $26,900 for 42 days, in Canadian dollars. The centre itself gives prices over the phone at 604-947-0420 or 1-866-233-2299. It says GST, meals, family programming and alumni meetings are included, while prescribed medications and a small weekly drug-testing fee are extra.

faqs.q: How long does treatment at the Orchard Recovery Center last?
faqs.a: Treatment at the Orchard Recovery Center can last 12, 28 or 42 days, depending on the individual’s needs. They offer flexible lengths of stay to ensure that each person receives the necessary support to achieve long-term recovery.

faqs.q: Does Orchard Recovery Center offer detox?
faqs.a: Yes, it offers on-site medical detox for alcohol and certain drugs. An addiction medicine doctor assesses you on arrival and prescribes a detox protocol, and nurses support you through withdrawal. The centre accepts people already taking methadone or Suboxone, but the 12-day stay is not suitable for opiate withdrawal or severe alcohol withdrawal.

faqs.q: Where is Orchard Recovery Center and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 811 Grafton Road on Bowen Island, a 20-minute BC Ferries ride from Horseshoe Bay in West Vancouver. Plan to take the 9:05 or 10:15 am sailing, because new clients must arrive before noon and intakes run on Mondays and Wednesdays. Walk on as a foot passenger and a staff member will meet you at Snug Cove. The centre does not do airport pickups, but a taxi or rideshare from YVR to Horseshoe Bay takes about 30 to 45 minutes.

faqs.q: What happens after I leave the Orchard?
faqs.a: You leave with an aftercare plan built with your counsellor and recovery coach. Alumni benefits come with the 28 and 42-day programs and include weekly then monthly check-ups for a year, 24/7 phone support, a daily online check-in from Monday to Friday and weekly alumni meetings on Zoom. Friends of the Orchard meetings also meet in Calgary and Victoria.

faqs.q: Is Orchard Recovery Center publicly funded?
faqs.a: No. The Orchard is a private, self-pay centre and has no government-funded beds, so Vancouver Coastal Health and the other BC health authorities do not pay for a stay there. The centre says its primary program can be claimed as a medical expense on your income tax. If you need a publicly funded option, call 811 or ask the Orchard's admissions team for a referral.

faqs.q: Does the Orchard Recovery Center accept insurance?
faqs.a: The Orchard Recovery Center is a private, self-pay centre, so it does not bill a public plan. Your private insurance provider, Employee Assistance Plan, extended health benefits, union or guild may fully or partially cover the cost of treatment, and admissions can talk through how they work with insurers.
